# Database inventory

Stage A (read-only) audit, 2026-11-02. Source: static scan of `database/migrations/0001`-`0135` (135 files), `libs/core/src/lib/database/*`, `docs/database/README.md`, `docs/runbooks/database-roles.md`. No database was connected to; nothing was executed against PostgreSQL. Status words: Verified (read in SQL/code), Not verified (not examined, or needs a live database).

## 2. Role and grant model (Verified: 0109, docs/runbooks/database-roles.md)

- `healthcare_app` is a NOLOGIN group role (0109:19-21). `apply_app_privileges()` (0109:23-60) grants `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on all tables, `USAGE, SELECT, UPDATE` on all sequences and `EXECUTE` on all functions in `public`; it revokes `TRUNCATE` everywhere, all writes on `schema_migration`, and `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on each table whose unconditional row-level `prevent_mutation()` trigger covers that action.
- The login role `healthcare_api` is created by hand (runbook step 3), never in source. `DATABASE_URL` is that role for API and both workers; `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` is the owner, used by the API pre-deploy `pnpm db:migrate` (`apps/api/railway.json` `preDeployCommand`; terraform `main.tf:29,48`).
- Migrator (`libs/core/src/lib/database/migrator.ts:20-75`) takes an advisory lock, applies each file in its own transaction, verifies checksums (LF-normalised; the raw checksum is also accepted), then runs `ensure_audit_partitions(3)`, `apply_rls_policies()`, `apply_app_privileges()`.
- Default when `secrets.app_database_url` is unset: API and workers run as the owner (terraform `main.tf:142-151`; runbook "Until it exists, everything runs as the owner"). See DB-001.

## 3. Row-level security

### 3.1 Mechanism (Verified, 0111)

`rls_organization_visible(uuid)` (0111:15-19; plain SQL, STABLE, not SECURITY DEFINER) is true when `app.scope = 'all'`, or when `app.scope = 'organization'` and the row's organization equals `app.organization_id`. Policies use `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` only. There is no `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, so the table owner bypasses them. Connections are stamped by `ContextPool` (`libs/core/src/lib/database/database-context.ts:92-135`) with session-level `set_config(..., false)` at every checkout.

### 3.3 Nullable `organization_id`

`role` (0004:32; CHECK `is_system = (organization_id IS NULL)`), `auth_session` (0004:87), `audit_event` (0110; its own policy: NULL rows readable only by the platform scope but writable by anyone). Tables the scanner listed as "nullable/PK" in section 7 with `organization_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES organization` (for example `patient_number_sequence` 0005:4, `staff_mfa_policy` 0086:21, `privacy_setting` 0114:24) are implicitly NOT NULL and get the strict policy. For genuinely nullable tables the generated policy is `USING (organization_id IS NULL OR visible) WITH CHECK (same)` (0111:50-52): an organization-stamped connection can also INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE the shared rows (DB-003).

## 4. Partitioning, retention and immutability

- `audit_event` is partitioned by month (Asia/Manila) from 0110: `audit_event_history` (pre-0110 data), `audit_event_default`, and monthly partitions kept three months ahead by `ensure_audit_partitions()`; TRUNCATE triggers on partitions (0110:77-78, 96). Archive and verified removal through `audit_archive` and `remove_audit_partition()` (0110:124-214).
- Append-only enforcement: `prevent_mutation()` row triggers on the tables marked in section 7, plus domain guard functions (`prescription_guard`, `lab_result_guard`, `billing_invoice_guard`, `medical_certificate_guard`, ...) that allow only defined transitions. The app role also loses UPDATE/DELETE on tables with an unconditional `prevent_mutation` trigger (docs: about 60 tables). Tables protected only by a conditional guard keep UPDATE/DELETE privilege and rely on the trigger.
- Core clinical tables with NO immutability trigger found and full DML privilege for `healthcare_app`: `patient`, `encounter`, `diagnosis`, `document`, `lab_order`, `lab_specimen`, `lab_order_item` (no `CREATE TRIGGER ... ON <table>` names them; grep of all migrations). FKs restrict deleting parents that have children, but the rows can still be edited or removed by the app role (DB-006).
- Merged-record protection: `refuse_record_for_merged_patient` INSERT triggers on patient-care tables (0068 onward).

## 5. Notable constraints and indexes

- Composite same-organization FKs `(organization_id, x_id)` throughout (docs/database/README.md "Conventions"; 898 `REFERENCES`).
- Exclusion constraints: `appointment_practitioner_no_overlap`, `appointment_room_no_overlap` (0009), `lab_reference_range_no_overlap` (0015), billing price effective ranges (0019).
- Money and stock integrity: `inventory_balance.quantity CHECK (>= 0)` (0026:89); `billing_account_entry` BEFORE INSERT balance trigger (0035:127-146) plus advisory lock `lockPatientAccount` (`libs/billing/src/lib/billing-support.ts:36-38`); `UNIQUE (organization_id, idempotency_key)` on `billing_payment` (0019:306) and `billing_payment_intent` (0038); `billing_charge_source_uq` (0019:135); `UNIQUE (organization_id, invoice_number)` (0019:166).
- Trigram indexes for patient search (0005): `patient_name_search_trgm_idx`, `patient_family_name_trgm_idx`.
- Per-organization numbers are rows updated with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` (`libs/patient/src/lib/patient-registration.service.ts:270-272`; `libs/billing/src/lib/catalog/billing-catalog.service.ts:354-356`), not PostgreSQL SEQUENCEs (gap-free, serialised by row lock).

## 6. PHI / PII data classes held in the database

| Domain                | Representative tables                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Class                                                                     |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Identity              | `patient`, `patient_identifier` (PhilHealth PIN, PhilSys, passport, senior/PWD ID, driver's licence, HMO id; clear text, 0005:49-66), `patient_contact_point`, `patient_address`, `patient_relationship`, `patient_qr_code`       | PII, government identifiers                                               |
| Clinical              | `encounter`, `encounter_note_revision`, `diagnosis`, vital signs, allergies, `prescription(_item)`, `clinic_procedure`, `immunization`, patient history tables, `reported_medication`, `external_history_entry`, `outside_result` | PHI; history includes substance use and sexual history (0082) = sensitive |
| Laboratory            | `lab_order`, `lab_result`, `lab_report_archive`, `lab_instrument_result`, `lab_send_out`                                                                                                                                          | PHI                                                                       |
| Dental                | `dental_tooth_state`, `dental_examination`, `dental_image`, `dental_perio_*`, treatment plans                                                                                                                                     | PHI                                                                       |
| Telemedicine          | consultation tables incl. `telemedicine_message` (chat text)                                                                                                                                                                      | PHI                                                                       |
| Messaging and records | `patient_message(_attachment)`, `records_request(_*)`, `medical_certificate`, `document`, `document_signature` (signature strokes)                                                                                                | PHI                                                                       |
| Billing               | `billing_invoice*`, `billing_payment`, `billing_account_entry`, `philhealth_*`                                                                                                                                                    | PII + financial                                                           |
| Portal and auth       | portal accounts, `auth_session`, `app_user`, trusted devices, passkeys, MFA secrets (encrypted with `MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), `push_subscription`                                                                                    | credentials, PII                                                          |
| Integration           | `integration_exchange` (digest only), sealed payload columns (AES-256-GCM key ring), `fhir_import_content` (sealed)                                                                                                               | PHI, column-encrypted                                                     |
| Ops / CRM             | `notification` (destination phone/email; no message body column in 0007), `crm_*`                                                                                                                                                 | PII                                                                       |
| Cached responses      | `idempotency_record.response_body`                                                                                                                                                                                                | PHI (DB-005)                                                              |

No application-level column encryption exists for identifiers, notes or results. Encryption at rest relies on the hosting provider's storage (Not verified); docs/database/README.md "Production hardening (not yet done)" lists encrypted backups and PITR as open.

## 7. All tables (generated)

Domain grouping is heuristic by name prefix. `org_id`: `yes` = NOT NULL column; `nullable/PK` = column exists but is nullable or is the primary key; `no` = absent. "Immutability trigger" lists trigger functions found on the table (regex over `CREATE TRIGGER`; may miss multi-line variants). A table with no entry can be updated and deleted by the application subject to FKs and CHECKs.

## Findings

The inventory itself is descriptive. Issues it surfaced are specified in full in POSTGRESQL_DATABASE_SECURITY_AUDIT.md and HEALTHCARE_DATA_PRIVACY_AUDIT.md; cross-references:

| ID      | Severity | Summary                                                                                                                                                                                | Status |
| ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| DB-004  | MEDIUM   | Patient-data child tables without `organization_id` or RLS (`prescription_item`, `care_plan_problem`, `care_plan_goal`, `care_plan_progress_note`)                                     | Open   |
| DB-005  | MEDIUM   | `idempotency_record` caches PHI response bodies, no purge job, no organization column                                                                                                  | Open   |
| DB-006  | MEDIUM   | Core clinical tables (`patient`, `encounter`, `diagnosis`, `document`, `lab_order`, ...) have no immutability trigger and the app role holds DELETE/UPDATE                             | Open   |
| DB-003  | MEDIUM   | Nullable-organization tables (`role`, `auth_session`) are writable by every organization context                                                                                       | Open   |
| INV-001 | INFO     | Counts in section 1 come from regex scans of SQL text, not from a live catalog; run the catalog queries in backup-and-restore.md "Checks" on a restored copy to confirm (Not verified) | Open   |
